Subject: Acme - Post-demo recap + proposed competitive bakeoff plan

Jamie / Priya / Rob —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment for the competitive bakeoff:

Summary of today
- Objective: validate inference economics and latency for Acme's customer-facing summarization pipeline (avg doc length ~1.2k tokens).
- Redwood value props to test: dedicated throughput, prefix/KV cache effectiveness, model-variant fallbacks, and cost/per-token under typical load.

Proposed bakeoff scope (see attached "+acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx+")
1) Baseline: your current hyperscaler setup (SageMaker/Azure/Google) running your prod model variant and input profile.
2) Redwood hosted + dedicated runs: equivalent model family + 8-bit quantized variant.
3) Failure/fallback scenarios: simulate capacity spike + automated fallback to cheaper variant.

Success criteria (please confirm):
- P95 latency (cold): <= 550ms for median requests; P95 steady-state <= 250ms
- Cost per 1k tokens: at least 20% improvement vs hyperscaler baseline
- Quality: <2% regression on your downstream ROUGE/QA checks vs prod baseline

Owners / timeline (proposed)
- Technical contact (Acme): Jamie Turner (you) + Rob Lee (infra) — provide baseline logs and prod input sample by Wed 8/19
- Redwood engineering owner: Aditya Rao — will own test harness and run environment config
- Redwood solutions (me) — coordinate schedule, SOW, and procurement points
- Kickoff: Tue 8/20 10:00 PT (30m) — agree?

Attachments: acme-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx (test matrix + data needs)

Requested asks for next steps
1) Please confirm the success criteria above or suggest changes.
2) Share a one-week sample of production inputs (anonymized) and a copy of your current infra runbook (SageMaker/Azure config).
3) Confirm kickoff time (proposed 8/20 10:00 PT).

Happy to hop on a quick sync if you'd rather walk through the plan live. Thanks — excited to get this running.

Best,

Jamie — quick technical notes to help frame the test matrix. Attaching a short comparison PDF (redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf).

Key differentiators to validate during the bakeoff:
- Latency & cold-starts: Redwood’s serving runtime keeps a warmed KV cache for frequent prefixes and supports continuous batching; expect lower P95 on steady-state for streaming-heavy loads.
- Cost: quantization + kernel selection gives consistent per-token cost savings; we’ll log the cost breakdown token-by-token to show delta vs your baseline.
- Determinism & fallbacks: Redwood supports pinned model variants and automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant when dedicated capacity is saturated — we should simulate both graceful degradation and hard-failure to compare availability.
- Observability: our Console exposes token-level latency and cost traces and integrates with your monitoring via Datadog/Push metrics.

Proposed minimum test steps (technical owner in parens):
1) Baseline capture (Acme - Rob) — 1 week aggregated prod sample + a 2-hour synthetic replay for load tests.
2) Redwood hosted run (Redwood - Aditya) — match model family, record token-level traces.
3) Dedicated run with quantized variant (Redwood - Aditya) — enable KV cache and batching; measure cost and P95.
4) Spike test + fallback (Acme/Redwood joint) — simulate 3x traffic for 15 minutes; measure fallback success and availability.

Notes on success criteria instrumentation:
- We’ll provide a shared dashboard link (temporary) with P50/P95/P99, cost per 1k tokens, and quality regression numbers (we’ll accept your ROUGE/QA checks as the gold standard).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-comparison.pdf (1 page)

I’ll prep the test harness and a small script to replay sample traffic; Marissa — if you can share the sample and logs, I’ll start configuring the runs.

—Aditya
